key_insight: Combining Fourier features, complex-valued learning, and Navier–Stokes constraints enables flow reconstruction across large unobserved regions despite noisy measurements.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help recover velocity, pressure, and vorticity fields when flow measurements are sparse, noisy, or obstructed.
method: Fourier features represent oscillatory and multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued representations support coupled amplitude–phase learning.
Convolutional residual blocks enforce Navier–Stokes physics.
evidence_signal: Tests cover Taylor–Green and cylinder-wake flows at Re=100, three severe wake-gap geometries, robustness to Gaussian noise up to 20%, and lower errors than a conventional PINN on forced 2D Kolmogorov turbulence with 5% Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Performance on three-dimensional, higher-Reynolds-number flows and experimental measurements remains unestablished by the reported evaluations.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
